newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican left keeps big lead in capital race - poll.
newsitem.headline: Mexican left keeps big lead in capital race - poll.

text.p: Veteran left-winger Cuauhtemoc Cardenas retains a commanding lead over his two nearest rivals in the race to be elected Mexico City's mayor, one of Mexico's most important posts, according to a new poll.

The poll, taken by the Indemerc/Louis Harris organisation and made available to Reuters by one of the sponsors on Monday, gave Cardenas 41 percent support for the July 6 election once "don't knows" and abstainers were excluded.
A similar poll by Indemerc taken in early March gave Cardenas and his Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) 40 percent.
Cardenas' nearest rival, conservative Carlos Castillo Peraza of the National Action Party (PAN), trailed with 26 percent in the latest Indemerc poll, down from 28.9 percent in March.

In third place came Alfredo del Mazo, running for President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), with 21 percent support. The other preferences expressed were for small fringe parties.
Indemerc surveyed a random sample of 800 electors for the poll, which it said had a margin of error of plus or minus three percentage points.
The campaign for the first-ever election of a mayor of Mexico City -- hitherto a job assigned directly by the president -- has become increasingly dirty in recent weeks.
But so far none of the mudslinging appears to have changed voters' minds, and Cardenas has retained the lead he took when he declared he would run.
